question.problem:
Let $(a,b)$ be the solution of the following system. What is the value of $a+b?$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.4a-0.8b-1.2=0 \\ 0.5a-1.5b-5=0\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of the decimals, we multiply both equations by $10,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}0.4a-0.8b-1.2=0 & |\,\times 10 \\ 0.5a-1.5b-5=0 & |\,\times 10\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}4a-8b-12=0 \\ 5a-15b-50=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that if we divide the first equation by $4$ and the second equation by $-5,$ we will get a $a$ term in the first equation that can cancel with the $-a$ term in the second equation:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4a-8b-12=0 & |\,÷(4) \\ 5a-15b-50=0 & |\,÷(-5)\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}a-2b-3=0 \\ -a+3b+10=0\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the two equations eliminates the $a$-variable and allows us to solve for $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\cancel{a}-2b-3 & =0 \\ -\cancel{a}+3b+10 & =0 \\ (-2b+3b)+(-3+10) & =0 \\ b+7 & =0 \\ b & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $b=-7$ into the equation $a-2b-3=0$ to solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a-2b-3 & =0 \\ a-2(-7)-3 & =0 \\ a+14-3 & =0 \\ a+11 & =0 \\ a & =-11\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-11$ and $b=-7.$ So, 

$$
a+b=-11+(-7)=-18.
$$
